decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already captures that only the shared terminal is under review while all other established geometry remains locked.

The existing MODIFY captures the new terminal and geometry constraint but leaves the obsolete requirement that the exact prior Hero V geometry remain wholly unchanged, despite the terminal now being revised.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

After comparing the kerning studies together, I am definitely most attracted to Option 2 (Balanced Flow). It reads as one unified word but still retains the airiness and elegance we have been developing.

Before proceeding with the material treatments, I want to reconsider the terminal used by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We devoted substantial time to perfecting the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet had been created. At that point, the Hero V had to express far more of the identity by itself. With the complete wordmark now assembled, I no longer think it needs to be so expressive or decorative.

I’m seeking a feeling of precision, assurance, and quiet elevation. I’d like to test a terminal that appears more deliberate and architectural—a restrained, controlled upward release instead of a flourish.

I’m attaching two references that start to convey the quality I mean. I do not want either one reproduced exactly, but their cleaner transitions and more restrained elevation appeal to me.

The established structure and slope of both the Hero V and second V should remain unchanged. Instead, please create a few interpretations that preserve that geometry while applying a consistently refined terminal to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

value_updates.master_geometry_role: The Hero V remains the system foundation, but its terminal should use a restrained architectural treatment applied consistently to the Hero V, second V, and É accent rather than functioning as an exclusive expressive flourish.
value_updates.terminal_style: a deliberate, architectural, restrained, and controlled upward release rather than an expressive or decorative flourish
value_updates.geometry_preservation_constraint: Preserve the established Hero V structure and slope while refining only the terminal.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY fully captures the refined terminal and preservation of the second V's established structure and slope.
The source changes the terminals of the Hero V, second V, and É accent only; it does not require a change to the E or L letterforms.
The terminal study preserves the second V's established structure and does not change its height relationship to the E, L, Hero V, or É accent.
The existing same-message MODIFY captures the new terminal style, while the requirement that the accent literally derive from and correspond to the Hero V terminal remains valid.
The source selects Option 2 Balanced Flow, and the candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording that selection.
The client postpones proceeding with material work until the terminal study is reviewed but does not change the selected Satin Reflection finish or its required character.
Refining the shared terminal does not alter the existing requirement that the Hero V and É accent peaks align on the same horizontal reference line.
The terminal study does not change which signature elements receive champagne gold or the black treatment of the remaining elements.
The request for comparative terminal interpretations does not modify the standing requirement to explain the design focus of each round.
The terminal-study decision has no effect on the accepted file formats for review images.
